subject: axolotl
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: axolotl with frilly pink gills.
Style: chibi.

spec.name: Chibi Axolotl
spec.description: A chibi leucistic axolotl: a huge flat smiling head, a stubby pale-pink body, a paddle tail with a frilled fin and six feathery hot-pink gills, standing in a neutral rest pose.
spec.layout: UNITS ARE METERS, life-size axolotl (about 0.5 m with gills, tail and head). The model faces +Z, +X is the model's left, and it stands on y=0. The model is a low, wide salamander with a chibi head about 2x as wide as the body. Seen from the front: a very wide, flat, rounded head (width 0.2, height about 0.13) with two big black bead eyes high on the top corners, pink cheek blushes, a wide upturned smile and two tiny nostril dots. Three hot-pink gill stalks sprout from each rear cheek and fan sideways and up, carrying dense frilly filaments, so the gills span about x=±0.19 and are the loudest silhouette feature. The chunky body (width 0.13, height 0.10) lies behind the head and rests its belly on the floor. Four stubby limbs splay sideways with flat paws; each paw has long, rounded finger and toe tips fanned forward (4 digits on the hands, 5 on the feet). A laterally flattened tail tapers back to z=-0.31, with a scalloped fin running from behind the head along the back and round the tail tip, plus a short ventral fin on the tail. SKULL GEOMETRY (shared by head, face and gills): the upper skull is an ellipsoid centred at headCenter [0,0.083,0.14] with radii x 0.10, y 0.057, z 0.09 (top y=0.14, front z=0.23, rear z=0.05). The lower jaw is an ellipsoid centred at [0,0.035,0.15] with radii [0.088,0.026,0.078], hinged at jawHinge. The mouth seam sits at about y=0.056. The head ellipsoid is the only surface the face and gills seat on, so those parts must snap their details with b.surface(b.root).nearest(point) or .around(headCenter).at(az, el). Skull parts are built first, and the build order is head, face, gills, bodyTail, limbs. STYLE: stubby, rounded and cute, with chunky bold shapes, flat colours and low-poly facets (6 to 10 sided tubes, 8x6 spheres). Colour by place: pale rose on top, a cream belly and underjaw, darker rose back patch and freckle spots, then a deep-rose to hot-pink to pale-pink gradient along each gill filament. Fine detail (eyes, shine, blush, freckles, toe tips, fin ribs) is small separate parts in their own colours. Everything is left-right symmetric. Do not add a ground, rocks or water.

parts.builds: The chibi skull and jaws, which together read as one very wide, flat, rounded head. (1) Upper skull ellipsoid at headCenter with radii [0.10,0.057,0.09] in skin, shaded by a darker skinBack cap over the crown (a slightly smaller ellipsoid or flat lathe on top, y>0.1) and a few spot-coloured freckle discs seated on the crown (use b.surface/stick). (2) A snout bump: a small flattened ellipsoid at [0,0.07,0.205] so the front is blunt and cute. (3) Lower jaw on joint jaw: ellipsoid centred [0,0.035,0.15] with radii [0.088,0.026,0.078] in belly/cream, with a skin-coloured upper rim, so the mouth seam sits at y≈0.056. Inside the mouth, a small dark mouthInside tray on the upper skull's underside and a tongue (flat tongue-coloured ellipsoid) on the jaw floor. Both jaws overlap enough that the closed mouth has no gap. (4) Two low brow ridges above the eyes (small skin-coloured ellipsoids at eyeL/eyeR raised 0.012) so the eyes sit under a bump. (5) The throat/gular fold: 2 thin cream arcs under the jaw. Faceted low-poly spheres (10x7).
parts.attaches: Rides joints head (skull) and jaw (lower jaw, tongue). The back of the skull overlaps the body front at neckJoin. The gills and face build onto this skull surface at the mounts gillBase* and eyeL/R, cheekL/R and nostrilL/R.

parts.builds: Every facial detail, seated on the skull surface (snap with b.surface(b.root).nearest or b.stick; the head part is already built). (1) Two big chibi eyes at eyeL/eyeR, each layered: a dark eyeRing sphere (r 0.019), an eye bead sphere (r 0.016, glossy near-black), a thin eyeGold ring or crescent just under the pupil, and two white shine spots (one large at the upper outer side, one tiny lower inside) with r 0.005 and 0.0025. Eyes bulge slightly out of the skull and face forward-up. (2) A wide upturned smile: a mouthLine sweep (r 0.0012) draped along the mouth seam from the corner at x=-0.085 to x=+0.085, with both ends curling up 0.01, plus tiny dimple ticks at the corners. The line rides jaw/head and does not cover the jaw seam. (3) Blush: flat blush-coloured ellipses (about 0.03x0.02, 0.002 thick) at cheekL/R, aimed outward, plus 3 tiny darker blush ticks on each. (4) Nostrils: two tiny nostril-coloured dots at nostrilL/R. (5) A few tiny spot-coloured freckles across the snout. (6) A thin dark eyeRing arc brow lines above each eye. Everything stays small, layered as outline, main colour and highlight, and nothing hangs in front of the face.
parts.attaches: Seats on the head skull (head part) at eyeL/R, cheekL/R, nostrilL/R and mouthFront. The smile and mouth details are placed along the jawHinge seam and ride joint head for the upper features and joint jaw for the lower lip ticks.

parts.builds: The signature frilly gills: 3 stalks per side (6 total), the richest part of the model. Each stalk starts at gillBase{L,R}{1,2,3} (sunk slightly into the skull) and follows the joints gill{L,R}{n} and gill{L,R}{n}b (about 0.09 to 0.11 m long). Stalk directions are: stalk 1 out, up and back (reaching about y=0.2), stalk 2 out and a little up (reaching x≈±0.175), stalk 3 out and slightly down (low, nearly horizontal). Each stalk is a tapered smooth-skinned sweep (radius 0.007 to 0.003) on its two joints (gillStalk, with a darker gillDeep base collar of 0.01 radius where it meets the head). Along each stalk, 6 to 7 pairs of filaments branch both ways, built as slim leaf-shaped extrudes or flattened tapered spikes (length 0.03 near the base, 0.045 mid-stalk, shrinking to 0.02 at the tip), fanned about 50° to 70° away from the stalk, and curved a little backward. Filament colour runs root to tip: gillDeep or gillStalk, then gillFrill, then a gillTip pale-pink point or tiny bead. The filaments of the upper stalks arch up and those of the lower stalks droop, and the sides are slightly different lengths so the fan reads full and feathery. Each filament rides its stalk joint, so the gills can wave. A small cluster of 3 short filaments finishes each stalk tip. Mirror exactly across x=0. Use faceted 5-6 sided tubes.
parts.attaches: Roots at the mounts gillBaseL1-3 and gillBaseR1-3 on the rear cheeks of the skull ellipsoid (centre headCenter). Joints gill*, gill*b are children of head.

parts.builds: The torso, tail and fins. (1) A chunky body loft (chain/sweep over hips, spine and the neckJoin point) from z≈0.07 to z=-0.11, about 0.13 wide and 0.10 tall with a rounded oval section. It is centred at y=0.05 so its belly bottom rests on y=0, in skin, with a cream belly sector underneath (sectors or a separate flatter belly sweep) and a darker skinBack stripe sector along the back. (2) The tail is a swept chain on tail1..tail5 starting at tailRoot with the same section as the body end (half-width 0.045, half-height 0.045) and tapering to a flat paddle at tailTip (half-width 0.006, half-height 0.016) with a round or point cap, laterally flattened (taller than wide), cream belly sector underneath. (3) The dorsal fin: a membrane or extruded scalloped ridge from dorsalStart (just behind the head) along the back and the full tail round the tip, 0.025 high on the body rising to 0.035 on the tail, then falling to a rounded tip, in fin colour with a finEdge rim strip (a thin sweep along its outer edge), small rib lines (thin finEdge extrudes or rods) every 0.02, and scalloped bumps along the edge. A shorter ventral fin underneath the last 0.12 m of tail, same style. The fin rides the tail joints. (4) Markings: 10 to 14 spot-coloured freckle discs scattered on the back and tail sides (b.surface scatter, minDist 0.025), size 0.006 to 0.012. (5) Subtle details: a cloaca bump (belly-coloured, 0.01) underneath at z=-0.1 and 4 to 5 faint costal groove arcs (thin skinBack rods wrapped on each flank). All sweeps bend smoothly at the joints.
parts.attaches: The front end overlaps the back of the head skull at neckJoin [0,0.055,0.06]. Limbs attach to its flanks at shoulderL/R and hipSocketL/R. The gills and face do not touch it. Joints are hips, spine and tail1 to tail5.

parts.builds: Four stubby, splayed limbs with chunky paws and long rounded digits. Front limbs run shoulder{L,R} to elbow{L,R} to hand{L,R}, and hind limbs hip{L,R} to knee{L,R} to foot{L,R}, using the joint positions exactly. Each limb is a smooth sweep, radius 0.016 at the root tapering to 0.012 at the wrist or ankle, in skin with a pale belly-coloured underside and a small spot freckle or two on each upper arm. Each limb root is hidden by a rounded skin shoulder or hip bulge ellipsoid (r≈0.022) seated on the flank at shoulder{L,R} and hipSocket{L,R}. Paws: a flat, rounded palm pad (flattened ellipsoid, 0.032 wide, 0.008 thick, resting on y≈0.004 to 0.012 so the underside touches the floor around y=0) at handPad{L,R} and footPad{L,R}, with a darker pad-coloured sole patch. Digits: 4 per hand (fingerL1-4, fingerR1-4) and 5 per foot (toeL1-5, toeR1-5), each a 6 to 7 sided tapered capsule or sweep from the digit joint along its dir (length 0.022 to 0.03, radius 0.0048 tapering to 0.003 and ending with a round tip), fanned as per the joint directions, lying flat on the floor (centre y≈0.006) and the outer and inner digits slightly shorter. Each digit ends in a small digitTip-coloured bulb (r≈0.004). Digits ride their digit joints, and arm and leg tubes ride their chain joints. Everything mirrored across x=0.
parts.attaches: Roots at shoulderL/R and hipSocketL/R on the body flanks (bodyTail) and ends at handPad* and footPad* mounts on the floor. The chains parent to spine (arms) and hips (legs).

calls.reasoning:
I'm figuring out dimensions for a chibi axolotl design, scaling down a real axolotl's roughly 25cm length into small proportions with frilly pink gills, aiming for something around 0.3-0.4 meters including the tail.

Facing +Z, I'm laying out the body: a big chibi head up front with large eyes and a smiling mouth, a short plump body, a tapering flattened tail with a dorsal fin, and four stubby legs with little digit details. I'm calculating total length from head to tail tip (~0.52m) and sketching out the part breakdown starting with head features like skull, jaw, eyes, nostrils, and blush spots.

For gills, I'm planning six frilled stalks (three per side) mounted at the back sides of the head, each with its own joint for a fan-like motion. Then splitting the rest into body/tail (spine, tail segments, dorsal fin, belly spots, tail fin membrane) and limbs (four legs with digit joints), landing on five total parts: head, face details, gills, body-tail, and limbs, with the face attaching via a joint to the head.

I need to precisely define the head's surface geometry since the face builder needs mounting points for eyes without direct access to how the head was constructed. I'm specifying the head skull as an ellipsoid with defined radii and center position, and deciding that parts build in listed order so the face part can reference the already-built head surface to position features analytically.

Now I'm mapping out the skeleton: a hips root joint, a spine joint above it, a head joint (no separate neck for this chibi design), and a jaw hinge joint parented to the head. I'm also planning a tail chain of several joints extending backward from the hips, descending slightly in height as they go.

Next I'm working out the gill stalks parented to the head, using a "fan" role for the base joints, with roughly six stalks each getting a base plus tip joint for about twelve joints total. Then I'm moving on to the leg chains, starting with front shoulder joints branching from the spine down through elbow and hand joints.

Now I'm planning the digits: four fingers per front hand and five toes per hind foot, each with two joints, named with L/R suffixes like fingerL1 and toeR1, all parented to their respective hand or foot joints. With everything under the joint budget, I'm starting to set actual body dimensions in meters, placing the belly near floor level.

I'm now working out exact coordinates for the body loft cross-section and leg placement—stubby chibi-style legs with shoulders, elbows, and hands/paws positioned so feet rest flat on the floor, splaying digits outward.

For the head, I'm sizing it as a wide, flat ellipsoid relative to the body to emphasize the chibi proportions, settling on radii that make it noticeably larger than the torso while keeping the bottom near floor level.

I'm splitting the skull into an upper cranium dome and a separate lower jaw wedge pivoting at the mouth line, so together they read as one rounded snout shape even though they're built as two pieces.

For the eyes, I'm placing small black bead spheres on the upper-side surface of the head ellipsoid, checking that their position satisfies the ellipsoid equation so they sit flush against the curved skull.

I'm working out facial feature placements: pink blush ovals on the cheeks, a smile curve along the mouth seam that turns up at the corners, and tiny nostril dots positioned by solving for the exact surface height on the head ellipsoid at that x,y location.

Now I'm computing where the gill bases sit on the back sides of the head, finding the azimuth and elevation direction vectors, then scaling to land exactly on the ellipsoid surface.

My ellipsoid math isn't converging cleanly for the gill base positions, so I'll just snap them onto the skull surface approximately rather than computing exact intersection points — using nearest-point-on-surface logic in the builder instead of precise trig.

Computing L3 at (0.087,0.059,0.117), giving final positions for the three gill mounts. I'm setting their outward directions and lengths—L1 angled up-and-back around 0.09 long, L2 more horizontal around 0.1, L3 angled down-and-back around 0.08—then planning each stalk to carry 6-7 pairs of frills.

Now I'm working out the gill size envelope (0.38, 0.21, 0.52) from the span and tip calculations, then moving to the tail chain, laying out joint positions stepping back in z from the hips at roughly 0.05 increments.

I'm tapering the tail height and width toward the tip for a laterally compressed paddle shape, while planning dorsal and ventral fin membranes running from behind the head along the back to the tail tip with a frilly scalloped edge, leaning toward a pale pink-cream translucent coloring with a leucistic white-pink body.

Settling on a leucistic color scheme: pale pink-cream body, cream belly, hot pink gills, with darker pink freckle spots on the back. I'm budgeting part counts across head, face, gills, body/tail, and limbs to stay under the 900 limit, then starting to lay out the joint hierarchy with a hip root and spine chain.

I'm working through joint positions and directions for hips, spine, head, and jaw, figuring out where the jaw hinge should sit relative to the mouth seam, then moving on to defining the tail joint attached to the hips.

I'm plotting a chain of tail segments trailing backward, which pushes the overall body length to about 0.54 in size, then starting on the front leg joints from shoulder to elbow to hand.

Now I'm fanning out four finger digits from the hand point, spacing their positions and directions so they splay forward in a natural grip shape.

For the hind leg, I'm placing hip, knee, and foot joints with forward-outward orientation, then adding five toe digits fanned from the foot base across a range of forward angles.

I still need to mirror the entire limb and hand structure to the right side with negated x-coordinates, and add gill joints with base and tip segments both tagged with the fan role.

Still computing joint positions...

Still working out color and mount coordinates...

Trying another angle for wider-set eyes, I settle on placing the left eye around (0.056, 0.123, 0.18) with a radius of about 0.017, sunk slightly into the head for a chibi look — roughly a third of the head width, which feels appropriately big-eyed. Now I'm working out blush placement on the cheeks, testing a shallower angle to find a point further forward and down from the eye.

I land on a cheek position around (0.089, 0.066, 0.172), checking it clears the gill area nicely, then set a nostril point at (0.022, 0.1, 0.224). Shifting to the body, I'm defining the torso as a loft shape tapering between z=0.07 and z=-0.11, roughly 0.065 wide and 0.05 tall, sitting at a mid-height of 0.05 with the front tucked inside the head and a tail root mount near z=-0.10.

Now I'm adding mount points for the neck join and limb attachments, defining pads for hands and feet, then starting to lay out the actual body part boxes -- head, face, and jaw bounding boxes with their joint assignments, followed by the gill box with its own joint connections.

Continuing on, I'm sizing the bodyTail box to sit on the floor with hips, spine, and tail joints, checking that the dorsal fin clearance stays within the box height near the head. Then I'm defining the limbs box, also floor-anchored, with arm and leg digit joints, and noting the overall model height comes out to about 0.21.

Now I'm finalizing overall size [0.4, 0.21, 0.54] and planning the spec text to emphasize chibi style traits—stubby, big-headed, flat-colored, rounded, cute—while specifying build order: head, face, gills, bodyTail, limbs. I'm also working out how parts reference shared joints created by the builder, deciding to just describe using named joint handles, and I'm allocating part budgets: head 130, face 130, gills 240, bodyTail 150.

Now I'm laying out the full joint hierarchy, chaining tail segments to hips and limb joints down each arm and leg, mirroring the right side with negated x-values, and defining the direction vectors for each finger and toe to give the axolotl its characteristic long, thin, rounded digits.

Then I compute the specific direction vectors for the hand, elbow, shoulder, hip, knee, and foot joints by taking the offsets between consecutive joint positions, settling on a leg radius of about 0.014.
